bullets.title: Record Nasdaq Futures Short + No 80% Downside Volume Day in 2024
bullets.body: Asset managers and hedge funds have built the largest Nasdaq Futures short position in history, yet NYSE has not recorded a single 80% downside volume day this year — an event that hasn't happened over the prior 30 years. The two signals in combination suggest substantial positioning overhang against a backdrop of unusual underlying market resilience.

bullets.title: US Index ETFs Back at New Highs, But Semis and Transports Lag
bullets.body: Bespoke notes that pretty much all key US index ETFs have returned to new highs, while the semiconductor and transport sectors remain below recent peaks. The divergence from these traditional leading groups is flagged as a potential warning sign for the rally's durability.

bullets.title: Q2 EPS Growth Running +50.5% Y/Y as Earnings Season Winds Down
bullets.body: With Q2 reports largely complete, aggregate year-over-year EPS growth is tracking at +50.5%, per HedgeEye. Strong earnings delivery has been a key underpinning of the index rally back to all-time highs.

bullets.title: AAPL Upgraded to Buy at Rothschild Redburn, $400 PT
bullets.body: Rothschild Redburn upgraded Apple from Neutral to Buy, raising its price target from $260 to $400. The bull case rests on Apple's 2.55 billion-device installed base, strong customer retention, and the high-margin Services segment.

bullets.title: APP Price Target Cut to $440 from $500 at Benchmark
bullets.body: Benchmark reduced its price target on AppLovin to $440 from $500, representing a meaningful trim though still above current consensus levels.

bullets.title: CoreWeave Revenue Backlog Hits $104B, Nearly 2x Market Cap
bullets.body: CoreWeave's revenue backlog now stands at $104 billion, nearly double its current market capitalization, signaling robust forward demand for its AI infrastructure services.

bullets.title: NVDA Spectrum-X CPO Switches Enter Mass Production; 100k Units Forecast for 2027
bullets.body: NVIDIA's Spectrum-X co-packaged optics switches for scale-out deployments are officially in mass production, with forecasts of 15k units in 2026 scaling to 100k units in 2027. TSMC has expanded CPO inspection equipment capacity to support the ramp.

bullets.title: AWS Trainium 4 Ramp: 5M Units H2 2027, 12M Units 2028
bullets.body: AWS is projected to consume 5 million Trainium 4 units in H2 2027 and 12 million in 2028, with three configurations expected and two likely to incorporate NPO (next-gen processor) design. The scale of projected consumption underscores intensifying competition with NVDA in AI training silicon.

bullets.title: SNOW PT Raised to $385 at Jefferies
bullets.body: Jefferies raised its Snowflake price target to $385 from $310, one of the more aggressive upgrades in the software space this week.

bullets.title: SNAP Hits Session Low Down 15%
bullets.body: Snap shares extended losses to a session low of -15% intraday, with no additional catalyst detail provided beyond the headline move.

bullets.title: OKLO Upgraded to Overweight
bullets.body: OKLO received an upgrade from Equal Weight to Overweight, reflecting growing institutional interest in nuclear power enablers tied to AI data center energy demand.

bullets.title: META's $14B Data Center with BlackRock Exposes Lenders to Insurance Gap
bullets.body: META and BlackRock are co-developing a $14 billion data center, but the FT flags that the project exposes lenders to a significant insurance gap — a structural risk worth monitoring for the broader hyperscaler capex buildout.

bullets.title: AMAT PT Raised to $675 at Berenberg
bullets.body: Berenberg raised its Applied Materials price target to $675 from $575, citing a constructive outlook for semiconductor equipment demand.

bullets.title: BofA: Long Gold — $6.3B Weekly Inflow, Largest Since January 2026
bullets.body: BofA strategist Michael Hartnett reiterated the 'Anything But Dollar' thesis, calling gold the best hedge against dollar weakness, bond losses, and asset inflation. Gold funds attracted $6.3 billion last week, the largest inflow since January 2026.

bullets.title: Japan 10-Year Bond Yield Hits 30-Year High at 2.93%; BOJ Hike Odds Rise
bullets.body: Japan's 10-year JGB yield surged to 2.93%, the highest level since 1996, driven by yen weakness and inflation risks. Markets are pricing a higher probability of a Bank of Japan rate increase in September; one trader noted maintaining a long yen position against the USD.

bullets.title: Copper Hits All-Time Highs; London Supply Squeeze Intensifying
bullets.body: Copper rallied 1.1% to new all-time highs, with a London supply squeeze driving prices toward records. HedgeEye frames the move as consistent with a Quad 3 macro regime.

bullets.title: US-China Robotics Decoupling Underway; AI Chip and Rare Earth Spillover Risk
bullets.body: Bernstein says the FCC ban on foreign-made mobile robots marks the beginning of US-China robotics decoupling, with potential expansion to AI chip restrictions and investments. China could retaliate via data controls or rare-earth magnets, creating cross-sector risk.

bullets.title: Iran Ceasefire Expires; Hormuz Traffic Halts, Deal Odds Collapse to 13-16%
bullets.body: The 60-day US-Iran ceasefire deadline expired without a final agreement, with Strait of Hormuz traffic reported halting. Prediction markets on Kalshi put the odds of a nuclear deal at 13% by March 2027 and 15-16% through 2029, all sharply lower in recent weeks. Trump simultaneously claims a backchannel exists with IRGC officials and says he is 'in no hurry.'

bullets.title: China 5Y Bond Yield Crashes 7% to 20-Month Low; Retail Sales Cooling
bullets.body: China's 5-year bond yield fell 7% to a 20-month low, a macro recession signal, even as foreign reserves posted their largest quarterly rise in 12+ years ($74.7B in Q2). Chinese retail sales continue to cool and property development investment fell 19.2% year-over-year through July.

bullets.title: MLCC Tightening Seen as Potential Analog to Early NAND Hike Cycle
bullets.body: One trader noted shifting to MLCC (multilayer ceramic capacitor) positions over NAND exposure, citing price and supply tightening that resembles the early stages of a prior NAND price-hike cycle. Cautious on whether the cycle will fully replicate but sees passive component players as early beneficiaries.
